questions.question: What time of day do the people gather to bring their offerings?
questions.explanation: The people return 'the next morning' with their offerings.

questions.question: What surface is the dew drop balanced on when the child brings it?
questions.explanation: The child holds 'a small leaf' with a dew drop.

questions.question: When the king says the bottle 'holds nothing today', he is using:
options: a description of the bottle's emptiness
questions.answer: a description of the bottle's emptiness
questions.explanation: He is describing that the bottle is currently empty.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'thankful':
questions.explanation: Thankful = grateful.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'precious':
questions.explanation: Precious means valuable; opposite is worthless.

questions.question: 'Balanced' in the sentence 'a drop of dew was balanced on the leaf' means:
questions.explanation: Balanced here describes the dew drop staying steady on the leaf.

questions.question: Which adult character's offering is closest in spirit to the child's?
options: the goldsmith — both are physical objects
the poet — both are about something that doesn't last forever in the same form
questions.answer: the poet — both are about something that doesn't last forever in the same form
questions.explanation: The poet's words and the dew both refuse to be 'objects' in the usual sense — they exist as moments / breath.

questions.question: Why might the king have chosen the CHILD's gift over the adults'?
options: The child had no other option
The child saw past objects to a TIME — the present moment
questions.answer: The child saw past objects to a TIME — the present moment
questions.explanation: The dew represents an idea — the now — not just an object.

questions.question: Why might the moral of this story be useful in modern life?
options: So we appreciate small everyday moments instead of always wanting something more
questions.answer: So we appreciate small everyday moments instead of always wanting something more
questions.explanation: Modern life often pushes us toward acquiring more; this story is a reminder to live in the now.

questions.question: Pick the proper noun in: 'The boy met Aesop in Rome.'
questions.explanation: Aesop is a proper noun (specific person) AND so is Rome (specific place); from the options, Aesop is correct.

questions.question: Pick the COMMON noun in: 'My friend lives in Pune.'
questions.explanation: Friend is a common noun (a class of people).

questions.question: Identify the adjective in: 'The crystal bottle sparkled in the sun.'
questions.explanation: Crystal describes the bottle — adjective.

questions.question: Past tense of 'walk' is:
questions.explanation: Regular past tense — add -ed.

questions.question: Past tense of 'see' is:
questions.explanation: See is irregular: see → saw.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the past tense?
options: The child smiles at the king.
questions.explanation: 'Listened' is past tense; the others are present, present, future.

questions.question: Which sentence describes a precious MOMENT (not an object)?
options: My grandmother's silver bangle is precious.
Holding my baby brother for the first time was precious.
questions.answer: Holding my baby brother for the first time was precious.
questions.explanation: A first-time experience is a moment that cannot be replayed.

questions.question: The story takes place in modern times.
questions.explanation: The story begins 'Long, long ago' — it is set in the past.

questions.question: The four offerings (gold, words, rice, dew) are all EQUALLY valuable.
questions.explanation: The story decides the dew is the most precious.

questions.question: Fables often use simple stories to teach a moral.
questions.explanation: That is the very definition of a fable.

questions.question: Adjectives describe nouns.
questions.explanation: Definition of adjective.

questions.question: All English verbs form their past tense by adding '-ed'.
questions.explanation: Many verbs are irregular: bring → brought, see → saw, keep → kept.

questions.question: The poet brings ____ written on paper.
questions.explanation: Words are the poet's offering.

questions.question: The farmer brings a single grain of ____.
questions.explanation: Rice is the farmer's offering.

questions.question: Antonym of 'delicately' is ____.
questions.explanation: Delicate / gentle vs rough.

questions.question: 'Mumbai' is an example of a ____ noun.
questions.explanation: Specific place → proper noun.

questions.question: Past tense of 'speak' is ____.
questions.explanation: Speak is irregular: speak → spoke.

questions.question: Why is the goldsmith's gift NOT chosen as the most precious thing? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: (1) Gold can be stored, hoarded, and replaced; it lacks the unique fleeting quality of the dew. (2) Many things in life — moments of love, courage, kindness — cannot be bought with gold, so gold cannot be the MOST precious of all.
questions.explanation: Identifies why gold is good but not best.

questions.question: If a friend asked, 'What is the moral of A Bottle of Dew?', how would you explain it in two or three sentences?
questions.answer: The moral is that the present moment is the most precious thing of all because it cannot be saved, repeated or replaced. Gold and words can be stored; a moment cannot. So we should be thankful for each ordinary moment of our day, just as the king kept the bottle to remind himself.
questions.explanation: Concise statement of the moral.

questions.question: Use each word in a sentence: (i) precious, (ii) thankful, (iii) delicately.
questions.answer: (i) 'My old photograph album is precious to me.' (ii) 'I am thankful for the kindness of my teachers.' (iii) 'She placed the small bird back into its nest delicately.' (Many correct answers.)
questions.explanation: Vocabulary in context.

questions.question: Underline the COMMON nouns in this sentence: 'The wise king listened to the goldsmith, the poet and the child in the courtyard.'
questions.answer: Common nouns: king, goldsmith, poet, child, courtyard. (No proper nouns in this sentence — all the people are described by their roles, not by name.)
questions.explanation: Tests recognition of common-noun roles.

questions.question: Convert each sentence to past tense: (i) 'The king holds the bottle.' (ii) 'The child smiles at the king.' (iii) 'They walk to the courtyard.'
questions.answer: (i) 'The king HELD the bottle.' (ii) 'The child SMILED at the king.' (iii) 'They WALKED to the courtyard.'
questions.explanation: Hold → held (irregular); smile → smiled and walk → walked (regular).

questions.question: Imagine you are the FARMER. Write 2-3 sentences describing why you brought a grain of rice and what you felt when the king chose the dew.
questions.answer: Sample answer: 'I brought a single grain of rice because without rice, no one in our village would eat. To me that grain was the most precious thing — it kept us alive. When the king chose the child's drop of dew, at first I felt confused. Then I understood: the king was not asking what was MOST USEFUL, but what was MOST PRECIOUS — and a moment is even more delicate than a grain.' (Many correct answers; rubric: first-person voice + a reason for the offering + an emotional response.)
questions.explanation: Reframes the moral from a different character's perspective.

questions.question: Compare the four characters and their offerings in a TABLE-LIKE answer. For each character: name the character, name the offering, and explain in one line why they think it is precious.
questions.answer: Goldsmith — gold dust — gold has long been a measure of wealth. Poet — words on paper — words can outlast their writer; they have a kind of immortality. Farmer — grain of rice — without rice, life itself fails. Child — drop of dew — it cannot be stored or repeated; it represents the present moment.
questions.explanation: Tabular comparison of all four offerings and their meanings.

questions.question: Write a short paragraph (6-8 sentences) describing the MOST PRECIOUS MOMENT you remember. Use at least two adjectives and at least two past-tense verbs.
questions.answer: Sample: 'Last Diwali, my whole family came to my grandfather's small house. The garden was full of warm yellow lamps. We sat on the cool floor while my grandfather told us OLD stories he heard as a child. My little sister LAUGHED so much that she nearly dropped her sweet. My grandfather looked at me and SMILED a deep, kind smile. I felt my heart go warm. Even now, when I close my eyes, I can see those lamps. That night was the most precious moment I remember.' (Rubric: clear single moment + adjectives + past-tense verbs + emotional resonance.)
questions.explanation: Encourages writing in the same spirit as the story.

questions.question: Some readers say the moral of the story is unrealistic — 'gold and rice ARE more precious than a vanishing drop of dew because they help people in real life'. Do you agree? Justify your answer in 5-6 sentences.
questions.answer: Sample: 'I both agree and disagree. In real life, gold and rice ARE essential for survival and security; without them, we cannot live. So the practical reader is right that they are precious. But the story is not really comparing usefulness — it is comparing TIME with THINGS. A moment, once gone, is truly gone; gold can be earned again, rice can be grown again. So the dew represents something even more fragile than gold or rice. The story's moral is not that gold is worthless, but that we should not OVERLOOK the things that pass quickly. Both views can be true at once.' (Rubric: takes a position, considers BOTH sides, supports each.)
questions.explanation: Evaluative essay; rewards balanced reasoning.
